The twelve include B123, the arc B1037 declined to restore BECAUSE B125 refutes it, and B111, which B1037 dispositioned as SUBSUMED; a reader of the metadata cannot tell those from live arcs. THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT FROM BOTH SIDES: B1037 caught B123 BY READING A BODY, B1043 missed B564 because NO BODY SAID SO, and the graph is the thing that should have said so. DEFECT B, SELF-CORRECTING ARCS ARE UNREGISTERED: 35 FINDINGS carry a CORRECTION/REFUTED/WITHDRAWN banner BELOW their own headline and 31 have no docs/RETRACTIONS.md row, against that file's own rule that 'every future retraction adds its row in the PR that banks the correction'. THE INSTRUMENT: scripts/checks/supersession.py, registry docs/consolidation/SUPERSESSIONS.md, gate `supersession` (the 28th), FAIL-CLOSED, TRIAGED NOT CAPPED per B821/B823 -- failing only on untriaged LOAD-BEARING items (a superseded arc still cited, or a self-correction whose verdict is not PROVED), 21 of 72 candidates, with the remaining 51 PUBLISHED AS A MEASURED BACKLOG rather than hidden. IT REFUSES TWO THINGS: it does not triage all 72, which would mean writing 72 judgements without reading 72 bodies -- the claim-line sin it exists to name; and IT DOES NOT WRITE THE BACK-LINKS, because `supersedes` conflates REPLACES with EXTENDS and a mechanical rule would mark live arcs dead. The registry disposes in THREE directions: REPLACES (B123, B111, B408, B702), EXTENDS (ten, including the five above), and SELF-LABELLED (B731, B437, B385, B812, B331, B558, whose headlines already carry their own withdrawal so no reader is misled). 11 checks; 6 locks; 28 GATES GREEN; Gate 5 untouched; zero anchors; nothing to CLAIMS.md; no mathematics asserted or disturbed.
